scenario: 面试官让你先把 CTR 模型的特征按来源和更新方式分门别类,再谈存储与服务。
scenario_en: The interviewer wants you to categorize CTR features by source and update pattern before discussing storage and serving.
q: CTR 特征通常分成哪四大家族?
q_en: What are the four feature families for CTR?
why: 四大家族:用户特征(user_id、年龄段、30 天 CTR、类目亲和,基数可达十亿)、广告特征(ad_id、广告主类目、创意类型、bid)、上下文特征(时段、广告位、设备、槽位,来自请求本身、实时)、交叉特征(user_id×广告主类目,基数极高、需预计算或学 embedding)。四类的来源、基数、更新频率各不同,决定了各自的存储与服务方式。
why_en: User, Ad, Context, and Cross features — each differs in source, cardinality, and update frequency, which dictates how each is stored and served.
diagram:
flowchart TD F["CTR 特征"] --> U["用户
基数~十亿, 时/天更新"] F --> A["广告
基数~百万"] F --> C["上下文
来自请求, 实时"] F --> X["交叉
基数极高, 预计算/embedding"]
options: 训练集、验证集、测试集、线上集
用户特征、广告特征、上下文特征、交叉特征
数值特征、文本特征、图像特征、音频特征
整型、浮点、字符串、布尔四种数据类型
options_en: Training set, validation set, test set, online set.
User features, Ad features, Context features, Cross features.
Numeric, text, image, audio features.
Integer, float, string, boolean data types.
optionExplanations: 数据集划分不是特征家族,答非所问。
对;按语义来源分成用户/广告/上下文/交叉四类,每类的基数、来源、更新频率不同,直接决定存储与服务策略。
模态划分对广告 CTR 不合适,主体是类别与数值特征,不是图像音频。
数据类型是底层表示,不是按业务来源分的特征家族。
optionExplanations_en: Dataset splits are not feature families — off target.
Correct — by semantic source into User/Ad/Context/Cross, each with distinct cardinality, source, and update frequency driving storage and serving.
Modality splits do not fit ad CTR, which is mostly categorical and numeric, not image/audio.
Data types are low-level representations, not business-source feature families.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户对某广告类目的历史偏好强度,是需历史聚合的预计算用户特征。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Category affinity is a user's historical preference strength for an ad category, a precomputed user feature needing history aggregation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个类别特征可取的不同值的总数,如 user_id 基数可达十亿。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cardinality is the number of distinct values a categorical feature can take, e.g. user_id cardinality reaching a billion.

scenario: 单看用户特征和广告特征,模型抓不到「某类用户特别爱点某类广告」这种交互效应。
scenario_en: User and Ad features alone miss interaction effects like 'this user type especially clicks this ad type'.
q: 交叉特征解决什么问题,又带来什么代价?
q_en: What do cross features solve, and at what cost?
why: 交叉特征(如 user_id×广告主类目)捕捉单个家族看不到的交互效应,在 Wide & Deep 里是主要的记忆(memorization)机制。代价是它把特征空间组合式炸开、基数极高,这正是要用 embedding 去压的原因。
why_en: Cross features capture interaction effects individual families miss and are the main memorization mechanism in Wide & Deep, but they explode the feature space combinatorially, motivating embeddings.
tradeoff: 交叉特征(抓交互、强记忆) vs 组合爆炸(基数极高、需 embedding 压缩)
whenOtherWins: 如果两个字段之间没有真实交互(相互独立),硬造交叉只会加剧稀疏、白占空间,不如不做。
options: 交叉特征降低基数、节省存储,是压缩手段
交叉特征捕捉家族间交互效应、是 Wide & Deep 的记忆机制,代价是特征空间组合爆炸
交叉特征只用于图像输入,与类别特征无关
交叉特征让模型更快收敛,没有任何存储代价
options_en: Cross features lower cardinality and save storage — a compression technique.
Cross features capture cross-family interaction and are Wide & Deep's memorization mechanism, at the cost of combinatorial explosion.
Cross features apply only to image inputs, unrelated to categorical features.
Cross features make the model converge faster with no storage cost.
optionExplanations: 恰恰相反,交叉特征把基数组合式放大,是空间爆炸的来源不是压缩。
对;它抓「A 类用户 × B 类广告」这类交互,是 Wide 侧记忆的核心,但组合爆炸迫使我们用 embedding 压维。
交叉特征正是类别特征的组合,和图像无关。
它带来的是空间爆炸而非零代价,收敛速度不是它的核心作用。
optionExplanations_en: Opposite — cross features multiply cardinality and are the source of the explosion, not compression.
Correct — they capture 'user type × ad type' interactions, the core of Wide-side memorization, but the explosion forces embeddings.
Cross features are exactly combinations of categoricals, unrelated to images.
They cause an explosion, not zero cost, and convergence speed is not their core role.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两个类别特征的组合(如 user_id×广告主类目),捕捉单特征看不到的交互效应。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cross feature is a combination of two categoricals (e.g. user_id × advertiser_category) capturing interactions single features miss.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型直接记住训练中见过的具体特征共现模式(如某用户点某广告主),对应 Wide 侧。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Memorization is the model directly recalling specific feature co-occurrences seen in training (a user clicking an advertiser), the Wide side.

scenario: user_id 有十亿量级。若把它 one-hot 编码喂给模型,每个样本的这一维就是一个十亿长的 0/1 向量。
scenario_en: user_id is on the order of a billion. One-hot encoding it makes this one feature a billion-long 0/1 vector per sample.
q: 为什么 one-hot 高基数 ID 会崩,说明该怎么办?
q_en: Why does one-hot encoding a high-cardinality ID collapse, and what does it imply?
why: 十亿维 one-hot 每个样本约 4GB(10 亿 × 4 字节),而且极稀疏(每样本只有一个 1)、绝大多数 ID 每批很少出现。存不下也没法学,这正是要用 embedding 把每个 ID 映射成低维稠密向量的原因。
why_en: A billion-dim one-hot is ~4GB per sample and extremely sparse, so it neither fits nor trains — which is exactly why IDs are mapped to low-dim dense embeddings.
options: one-hot 只占几 KB,完全没问题,不需要改
one-hot 十亿维每样本约 4GB 且极稀疏,存不下也难学,所以要用 embedding 映射成低维稠密向量
one-hot 崩是因为它把数值特征也编码了,与基数无关
one-hot 没问题,问题只在于模型层数不够深
options_en: One-hot takes only a few KB and is fine, needing no change.
A billion-dim one-hot is ~4GB per sample and extremely sparse, so it neither fits nor trains — hence embeddings mapping IDs to low-dim dense vectors.
One-hot collapses because it also encodes numeric features, unrelated to cardinality.
One-hot is fine; the only issue is the model not being deep enough.
optionExplanations: 十亿维远不止几 KB,10 亿×4 字节≈4GB,单样本就压垮内存。
对;高基数+稀疏让 one-hot 每样本约 4GB 且几乎全零,既存不下又学不动,embedding 把它压成 16-64 维稠密向量。
崩的根因是类别基数太高,不是把数值也编码进来。
加深模型救不了输入表示爆炸,根子在 one-hot 的维度。
optionExplanations_en: A billion dims is far more than a few KB; 1B×4 bytes ≈ 4GB crushes memory for a single sample.
Correct — high cardinality plus sparsity makes one-hot ~4GB per sample and nearly all zeros, so embeddings compress it into 16-64 dense dims.
The collapse is from high categorical cardinality, not from also encoding numerics.
Deepening the model cannot fix an exploded input representation; the root is one-hot dimensionality.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一个类别值编码成只有对应位为 1、其余全 0 的向量;高基数时维度爆炸。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: One-hot encoding represents a category as a vector with a single 1 and the rest 0; at high cardinality the dimension explodes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在任一批数据里绝大多数取值都不出现的特征(如某个 user_id),向量几乎全零。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sparse feature is one whose values rarely appear in any batch (like a given user_id), making the vector nearly all zeros.

scenario: 你要把十亿量级的 user_id、百万量级的 ad_id 这类高基数类别特征喂进模型,又不能用 one-hot。
scenario_en: You must feed high-cardinality categoricals like billion-scale user_id and million-scale ad_id into the model without one-hot.
q: 该用什么表示,它凭什么既省空间又有用?
q_en: What representation should you use, and why is it both compact and useful?
why: 用 embedding:训练时把每个类别 ID 映射成一个 16-64 维的稠密向量,点击模式相近的 ID 学到相近的向量。它把十亿维稀疏压成几十维稠密,既存得下又让模型能在连续空间里泛化到相似 ID。
why_en: Use embeddings — map each ID to a learned 16-64-dim dense vector where similar click patterns give similar vectors, compressing billions of sparse dims into dozens of dense ones while enabling generalization.
tradeoff: embedding(几十维稠密、可泛化、需存表) vs one-hot(十亿维稀疏、存不下、不泛化)
whenOtherWins: 如果类别基数很低(如设备类型只有几种),直接 one-hot 更简单,没必要为它训 embedding。
options: 继续用 one-hot,只是把维度砍到一百万
用 embedding:把每个 ID 映射成 16-64 维稠密向量,相似点击模式→相似向量,压维且能泛化
把 ID 直接当整数标量喂进模型,省掉编码
对每个 ID 单独训练一个小模型,再集成
options_en: Keep one-hot but cut the dimension to a million.
Use embeddings: map each ID to a 16-64-dim dense vector, similar click patterns giving similar vectors — compact and generalizing.
Feed the ID directly as an integer scalar and skip encoding.
Train a separate small model per ID and ensemble them.
optionExplanations: 砍到一百万维仍是巨大稀疏 one-hot,没解决存储和泛化问题。
对;embedding 学出低维稠密表示,相似 ID 靠近,既把十亿维压到几十维,又让模型能对没怎么见过的 ID 泛化。
把 ID 当整数标量会强加一个虚假的大小顺序(id=5 不比 id=3「大」),模型学不到语义。
每个 ID 一个模型不可行(十亿个模型),embedding 才是可扩展表示。
optionExplanations_en: A million-dim one-hot is still huge and sparse, solving neither storage nor generalization.
Correct — embeddings learn low-dim dense representations where similar IDs sit close, compressing billions to dozens and generalizing to rarely-seen IDs.
Feeding the ID as an integer imposes a false ordinal (id=5 is not 'bigger' than id=3), so the model learns no semantics.
One model per ID is infeasible (a billion models); embeddings are the scalable representation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 训练中为每个类别 ID 学到的低维(16-64)稠密向量,相似 ID 向量相近,替代 one-hot。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An embedding is a learned low-dim (16-64) dense vector per categorical ID where similar IDs are close, replacing one-hot.

scenario: 你给十亿个用户各训一个 64 维 float32 的 embedding,要估算光这张表占多少内存。
scenario_en: You train a 64-dim float32 embedding for each of a billion users and must estimate the table's memory.
q: 这张用户 embedding 表的原始大小怎么算、约多少?
q_en: How do you compute the raw size of this user embedding table, and roughly how much?
why: 公式:行数 × 维度 × 每数字字节数 = 10 亿 × 64 × 4 字节(float32)= 256 GB。这是压缩前的原始基数,直接说明光一张用户 embedding 表就装不进单机内存,必须压缩+分片。
why_en: Rows × dims × bytes = 1B × 64 × 4 (float32) = 256 GB, the raw base showing one user embedding table alone won't fit a single node and needs compression plus sharding.
options: 10 亿 × 64 × 4 字节 = 256 GB(压缩前原始大小)
10 亿 × 4 字节 = 4 GB,维度不影响大小
64 × 4 字节 = 256 字节,与用户数无关
options_en: 1B × 64 × 4 bytes = 256 GB (raw, pre-compression).
1B × 64 × 4 bits = 32 GB.
1B × 4 bytes = 4 GB; dimensions do not affect size.
64 × 4 bytes = 256 bytes, independent of user count.
optionExplanations: 对;256 GB = 10 亿行 × 64 维 × 4 字节,这是压缩前基数,说明单机装不下、要量化+分片。
float32 是 4 字节不是 4 位,算成位少了 8 倍。
维度当然影响大小,漏乘 64 维少算了 64 倍。
总大小随用户数线性增长,不能只算单个向量。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — 256 GB = 1B rows × 64 dims × 4 bytes, the pre-compression base showing it won't fit one node and needs quantization plus sharding.
float32 is 4 bytes not 4 bits; using bits undercounts by 8×.
Dimensions do affect size; omitting the ×64 undercounts by 64×.
Total size grows linearly with users; you cannot count just one vector.

termDefinitions.meaning: 32 位(4 字节)单精度浮点数,embedding 默认的数值格式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: float32 is a 32-bit (4-byte) single-precision floating-point number, the default numeric format for embeddings.

termDefinitions.meaning: 存放所有类别 ID 各自 embedding 向量的大表,行数=基数,可达数百 GB。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An embedding table stores every categorical ID's embedding vector, with rows equal to cardinality, reaching hundreds of GB.

scenario: user_id 的 embedding 表有几十亿行,存不下。你想用一种不需要维护 ID→行号 映射表的办法把行数砍下来。
scenario_en: The user_id embedding table has billions of rows and won't fit. You want to shrink rows without maintaining an ID-to-row lookup.
q: 特征哈希(feature hashing)怎么压,代价是什么?
q_en: How does feature hashing compress, and at what cost?
why: 特征哈希用一个哈希函数把多个 ID 映射进同一个桶,把几十亿行压到几百万行(约 100:1),不用存 ID→行 的映射表。代价是哈希碰撞:不同 ID 共享一个 embedding 引入噪声,但量级可控。
why_en: Feature hashing maps many IDs into the same bucket via a hash, shrinking billions of rows to millions (~100:1) without a lookup table, at the cost of collisions that add manageable noise.
tradeoff: 特征哈希(免映射表、行数骤降) vs 哈希碰撞(不同 ID 共享向量、引入噪声)
whenOtherWins: 如果 ID 数量本就不多、且每个 ID 都需要独立表示不能混淆(如关键广告主),直接用完整 embedding 表更准,不必哈希。
options: 给每个 ID 分配唯一行号并维护映射表,行数不变但查得快
用哈希函数把多个 ID 映进同一桶,行数压到约 1/100,代价是碰撞引入噪声
把 embedding 维度从 64 降到 1,靠减维压表
只保留出现过的 ID,其余全删,做不到就报错
options_en: Assign each ID a unique row and keep a lookup table; rows unchanged but faster reads.
Hash many IDs into the same bucket, shrinking rows ~100:1, at the cost of collisions adding noise.
Cut embedding dimension from 64 to 1 to shrink the table by reducing dims.
Keep only seen IDs and delete the rest, erroring if impossible.
optionExplanations: 维护完整映射表行数没减,存不下的问题依旧,而且要额外存映射。
对;哈希把 ID 折叠进固定桶数,约 100:1 压缩且免映射表,碰撞让少数 ID 共享向量、引入可控噪声。
降维压的是列不是行;十亿行的问题靠减维解决不了,且 1 维几乎没表达力。
只留见过的 ID 无法应对新 ID,也没有系统性压缩比,不是哈希的做法。
optionExplanations_en: A full lookup table does not cut rows, so the fit problem persists and you also store the mapping.
Correct — hashing folds IDs into a fixed bucket count (~100:1) without a lookup, and collisions make a few IDs share vectors with manageable noise.
Reducing dims shrinks columns not rows; a billion-row problem is not solved by dims, and 1 dim has almost no expressiveness.
Keeping only seen IDs cannot handle new IDs and gives no systematic compression ratio — not hashing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用哈希函数把多个 ID 映射进固定数量的桶,免维护映射表地把 embedding 行数大幅压缩,代价是碰撞。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Feature hashing maps many IDs into a fixed number of buckets via a hash, shrinking embedding rows without a lookup table at the cost of collisions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两个不同 ID 被哈希到同一个桶,被迫共享一个 embedding,引入噪声。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hash collision is two distinct IDs hashing to the same bucket and sharing one embedding, introducing noise.

scenario: 少数高频 ID(热门广告主、活跃用户)贡献大部分曝光,长尾里海量 ID 各自只出现几次。你想把 embedding 的容量花在刀刃上。
scenario_en: A few high-frequency IDs (popular advertisers, active users) drive most impressions, while a huge long tail each appears a few times. You want to spend embedding capacity wisely.
q: 混合维度 embedding 怎么分配容量?
q_en: How do mixed-dimension embeddings allocate capacity?
why: 混合维度:给高频 ID 分配更大维度(如 64 维),给稀有 ID 分配小维度(如 16 维)。因为高频 ID 数据多、值得更强表示,长尾 ID 数据少、给大维度也学不满还浪费空间,把容量按频率分配。
why_en: Give frequent IDs larger dimensions (e.g. 64) and rare IDs smaller ones (e.g. 16), allocating capacity where data volume justifies it.
tradeoff: 混合维度(容量按频率分、省空间) vs 统一大维度(表达强但长尾浪费、表更大)
whenOtherWins: 如果 ID 频率分布很均匀、没有明显的头部和长尾,统一维度更简单,混合维度带来的复杂度不划算。
options: 所有 ID 一律给最大维度,保证表达力最强
高频 ID 给大维度(64)、稀有 ID 给小维度(16),按频率分配容量
高频 ID 给小维度、稀有 ID 给大维度,给冷门更多容量
所有 ID 一律给 1 维,极致压缩不管频率
options_en: Give every ID the largest dimension for maximum expressiveness.
Give frequent IDs large dims (64) and rare IDs small dims (16), allocating capacity by frequency.
Give frequent IDs small dims and rare IDs large dims, giving cold ones more capacity.
Give every ID 1 dim for extreme compression regardless of frequency.
optionExplanations: 统一大维度让海量长尾 ID 都占大空间却学不满,浪费内存。
对;高频 ID 数据多值得大维度,长尾 ID 数据少给小维度即可,容量随频率分配,省空间又不丢主力表达。
反了:稀有 ID 数据少,给大维度学不满、纯浪费,该把大维度给高频。
全 1 维丢掉了高频 ID 应有的表达力,过度压缩伤精度。
optionExplanations_en: Uniform large dims make the vast long tail occupy big space it cannot fill, wasting memory.
Correct — frequent IDs have data justifying large dims and rare IDs get small dims, allocating capacity by frequency to save space without losing the main expressiveness.
Reversed — rare IDs have little data, so large dims are wasted; large dims belong to frequent IDs.
All-1-dim strips frequent IDs of needed expressiveness, over-compressing and hurting accuracy.

termDefinitions.term: mixed-dimension embeddings / 混合维度嵌入
termDefinitions.meaning: 按 ID 频率分配 embedding 维度:高频给大维、稀有给小维,把容量花在数据多的 ID 上。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Mixed-dimension embeddings assign dims by ID frequency — large for frequent, small for rare — spending capacity where data is abundant.

scenario: 用户 embedding 表 float32 下约 256 GB,你想在几乎不改结构的前提下把它塞进更少内存。
scenario_en: The user embedding table is ~256 GB in float32, and you want to fit it in less memory with almost no structural change.
q: 量化(quantization)怎么压,256 GB 能降到多少?
q_en: How does quantization compress, and what does 256 GB drop to?
why: 量化把数值从 float32 降精度到 float16 或 int8,存储砍 2-4 倍:256 GB 用 int8 降到约 64 GB(1/4)。代价是精度略损,但 CTR embedding 通常能容忍,是最省事的压缩手段之一。
why_en: Quantization drops numeric precision from float32 to float16/int8, cutting storage 2-4×, so 256 GB becomes ~64 GB with int8 at a small accuracy cost.
tradeoff: 量化(存储砍 2-4 倍、精度略损) vs 保 float32(精度满、内存吃紧)
options: 量化把维度从 64 降到 16,256 GB 变 64 GB
量化把数值从 float32 降到 int8,存储砍约 4 倍,256 GB → 约 64 GB,精度略损
量化把行数减少 4 倍,256 GB → 64 GB,不损精度
量化增加精度到 float64,256 GB → 512 GB 换更高准确率
options_en: Quantization cuts dims from 64 to 16, turning 256 GB into 64 GB.
Quantization drops values from float32 to int8, cutting storage ~4×, 256 GB → ~64 GB, with a small accuracy cost.
Quantization cuts rows by 4×, 256 GB → 64 GB, with no accuracy loss.
Quantization raises precision to float64, 256 GB → 512 GB for higher accuracy.
optionExplanations: 降维是另一种手段(改列数),量化改的是每个数字的位宽不是维度。
对;float32→int8 每数字从 4 字节降到 1 字节,存储 1/4,256 GB→64 GB,代价是可容忍的精度损失。
量化不减行数(ID 还是那么多),减的是每个数值的精度位宽。
量化是降精度省空间,不是升到 float64,方向反了。
optionExplanations_en: Reducing dims is a different technique (columns); quantization changes each number's bit width, not dims.
Correct — float32→int8 drops each number from 4 bytes to 1, so storage is 1/4, 256 GB → 64 GB, at a tolerable accuracy cost.
Quantization does not cut rows (the IDs remain); it reduces each value's precision width.
Quantization lowers precision to save space, not raising to float64 — reversed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把数值从 float32 降精度到 float16/int8,存储砍 2-4 倍,精度略损。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Quantization lowers numeric precision from float32 to float16/int8, cutting storage 2-4× at a small accuracy cost.

termDefinitions.meaning: 8 位(1 字节)整数格式,量化常用,相比 float32 省 4 倍空间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: int8 is an 8-bit (1-byte) integer format common in quantization, 4× smaller than float32.

scenario: 十亿级 embedding 表超过了服务节点内存,你要列出可用的压缩手段。
scenario_en: A billion-scale embedding table exceeds serving-node memory, and you list the available compression techniques.
q: 以下哪些是压缩 embedding 表的有效手段?(多选)
q_en: Which are effective techniques to compress an embedding table? (multiple)
why: 四种有效手段:特征哈希(多 ID 共桶、约 100:1)、混合维度(高频大维、稀有小维)、量化(float32→int8、省 2-4 倍)、知识蒸馏(大 teacher 的 embedding 知识迁到小 student)。「加大 batch size」是训练超参,不压 embedding 表。
why_en: Feature hashing, mixed-dimension embeddings, quantization, and knowledge distillation all shrink the table, while increasing batch size is a training hyperparameter that does not.
options: 特征哈希——多个 ID 共享桶,约 100:1 压行数
混合维度 embedding——高频 ID 大维、稀有 ID 小维
量化——float32→int8 省 2-4 倍存储
加大训练 batch size——一次喂更多样本
options_en: Feature hashing — many IDs share a bucket, ~100:1 row shrink.
Mixed-dimension embeddings — frequent IDs large dims, rare IDs small dims.
Quantization — float32→int8 saves 2-4× storage.
Increase training batch size — feed more samples at once.
optionExplanations: 对;哈希把几十亿行折到几百万桶,约 100:1,是行数压缩主力。
对;混合维度按频率分配容量,长尾不再占大维,省列空间。
对;量化降位宽,int8 直接把表砍到 1/4。
错;batch size 是训练吞吐超参,和 embedding 表大小无关,不压表。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — hashing folds billions of rows into millions of buckets (~100:1), the main row compressor.
Correct — mixed dims allocate capacity by frequency so the long tail no longer takes big dims, saving columns.
Correct — quantization lowers bit width, and int8 cuts the table to 1/4.
Wrong — batch size is a training-throughput hyperparameter unrelated to table size and does not compress it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把大 teacher 模型的 embedding 知识迁移到更小的 student,以便在服务节点内存里放得下。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Knowledge distillation transfers a large teacher model's embedding knowledge to a smaller student so it fits serving-node memory.

scenario: LinkedIn 的 CTR 系统实践发现:不压缩 embedding,表就超出单个服务节点的内存。
scenario_en: LinkedIn's CTR system found that without compression the embedding table exceeds a single serving node's memory.
q: embedding 压缩为什么不是「锦上添花」而是「非做不可」?
q_en: Why is embedding compression a must, not a nice-to-have?
why: 不压缩,embedding 表放不进服务节点内存,实时推理就直接做不了——每次打分要查 embedding,查不到就没法在 10-20ms 内出 pCTR。压缩是让在线服务成为可能的前提,不是可选优化。
why_en: Without compression the table won't fit serving-node memory, so real-time inference is impossible — every score needs an embedding lookup — making compression a prerequisite, not an optional tweak.
options: 只是为了省点云成本,不压也能正常服务
不压缩表就放不进服务节点内存,实时推理直接做不了,压缩是在线服务的前提
压缩纯为提高模型精度,和内存/服务无关
压缩只影响训练速度,对线上服务没影响
options_en: It just saves some cloud cost; serving works fine without it.
Without compression the table won't fit serving-node memory, so real-time inference is impossible — compression is a serving prerequisite.
Compression is purely for model accuracy, unrelated to memory or serving.
Compression only affects training speed, not online serving.
optionExplanations: 不是省钱那么轻——放不进内存,服务根本起不来。
对;推理每次都要查 embedding,表超内存就查不了,10-20ms 出 pCTR 无从谈起,所以压缩是可行性前提。
压缩首先解决的是能不能放进内存、能不能服务,不是提精度。
它直接决定线上能否加载和查表服务,不只是训练速度。
optionExplanations_en: It is not mere cost saving — if it won't fit memory, serving cannot even start.
Correct — inference needs an embedding lookup each time, and an over-memory table cannot be queried, so 10-20ms pCTR is impossible, making compression a feasibility prerequisite.
Compression first addresses fitting memory and serving at all, not accuracy.
It directly determines whether the table can be loaded and served online, not just training speed.

termDefinitions.term: serving-node memory / 服务节点内存
termDefinitions.meaning: 承载在线推理的机器的内存容量,embedding 表必须放得下才能实时查表打分。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Serving-node memory is the RAM of the machine running online inference; the embedding table must fit for real-time lookup scoring.

scenario: 特征检索只有约 20ms 预算,你要给每个特征判定是预计算还是实时取。
scenario_en: Feature retrieval has only ~20ms, and you must classify each feature as precomputed or real-time.
q: 把「一个特征该预计算还是实时取」的判定推理排成正确顺序:
q_en: Order the reasoning for deciding whether a feature is precomputed or real-time:
steps: 问:这个特征需要跨会话/历史聚合吗(如用户 30 天 CTR)?
若需要历史聚合→预计算进特征库,在线只做 p99 <5-10ms 的快查
若能从当前请求直接得出(时段/设备/槽位)→实时从请求 payload 取,无需外部查
介于两者之间要秒/分钟级新鲜→用流式(Kafka+Flink)做中间地带
why: 判定原则:超出当前会话、要历史聚合的→预计算(在线快查);当前请求就能算出的→实时取(无外部查);要分钟级新鲜的→流式管线兜中间。这样把 20ms 预算花在必要的快查上,不在请求路径现算重聚合。
why_en: Aggregation beyond the current session is precomputed for fast lookup, request-derivable features are real-time with no lookup, and minute-fresh needs go through streaming as the middle ground.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  Q{"需历史聚合?"} -->|是| P["预计算→特征库快查"]
  Q -->|否, 请求可得| R["实时从 payload 取"]
  Q -->|需分钟级新鲜| S["流式 Kafka+Flink"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 用 Kafka+Flink 近实时聚合特征,延迟分钟级,是预计算(时/天)与纯实时之间的中间地带。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A streaming pipeline (Kafka+Flink) aggregates features in near-real-time (minutes), the middle ground between batch precompute and pure real-time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户一次连续使用的时段;会话内的状态可实时取,跨会话的历史需预计算。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A session is one continuous usage period; in-session state is real-time while cross-session history is precomputed.

scenario: 用户 30 天历史 CTR、类目亲和、user×广告主计数这类特征都要跨历史聚合,而在线只有 20ms 检索预算。
scenario_en: Features like user 30-day CTR, category affinity, and user×advertiser counts need history aggregation, but online retrieval has only 20ms.
q: 这类需历史聚合的特征该怎么在线服务?
q_en: How should such history-aggregation features be served online?
why: 预计算进特征库、在线只做 p99 读延迟 <5-10ms 的快查。批处理管线小时/天级刷新它们,若要分钟级新鲜(比如 3 分钟前点过某广告),用 Kafka+Flink 流式补齐。请求路径上绝不现算历史聚合。
why_en: Precompute into a feature store with a p99 read <5-10ms, refreshed by batch (hourly/daily) and bridged by streaming (Kafka+Flink) for minute-fresh needs, never aggregating history on the request path.
tradeoff: 预计算进特征库(在线 <5-10ms 快查、有新鲜度延迟) vs 请求路径现算聚合(最新但超 20ms 预算)
whenOtherWins: 如果特征完全由当前请求得出(设备、时段),就实时取、不进特征库;预计算只用于跨历史聚合量。
options: 每次请求现扫历史日志算聚合,保证绝对最新
预计算进特征库、在线 p99 <5-10ms 快查,批处理刷新,分钟级新鲜用 Kafka+Flink 流式补
把这些特征全丢弃,只用当前请求的上下文特征
让模型在推理时自己去数据库跑聚合查询
options_en: Aggregate by scanning history logs on every request for absolute freshness.
Precompute into a feature store with p99 <5-10ms lookup, refreshed by batch, and use Kafka+Flink streaming for minute-fresh needs.
Drop these features entirely and use only the current request's context features.
Have the model run aggregation queries against the database during inference.
optionExplanations: 请求路径现算历史聚合必然超 20ms 预算,扫日志根本来不及。
对;预计算+特征库快查守住延迟,批处理管日常刷新,Kafka+Flink 流式兜分钟级新鲜,分层解决新鲜度。
丢弃强历史特征白损精度;预计算就是为了既留住它又满足延迟。
推理时现跑聚合查询等于把重活放回请求路径,必超时。
optionExplanations_en: Aggregating history on the request path inevitably blows the 20ms budget; scanning logs cannot finish in time.
Correct — precompute plus feature-store lookup holds latency, batch handles routine refresh, and Kafka+Flink streaming covers minute-fresh, layering the freshness solution.
Dropping strong history features forfeits accuracy; precompute keeps them while meeting latency.
Running aggregation queries at inference puts heavy work back on the request path and must time out.

termDefinitions.term: p99 read latency / p99 读延迟
termDefinitions.meaning: 99% 的读请求都比这个值快,特征库常保证 <5-10ms 以守住在线预算。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: p99 read latency is the value 99% of reads beat; a feature store often guarantees <5-10ms to hold the online budget.

scenario: 时段、设备类型、广告位、槽位位置、以及本次会话已展示过哪些广告——这些信息在请求发生的一刻就都有了。
scenario_en: Time of day, device type, placement, slot position, and which ads were already shown this session — all available the moment the request happens.
q: 这类实时特征该怎么取,为什么不用预计算?
q_en: How are such real-time features obtained, and why not precompute?
why: 直接从请求 payload 和会话状态里取,无需任何外部查表。因为它们由当前请求就能得出、不需要跨历史聚合,预计算反而增加延迟和陈旧风险。原则:请求可得的实时取,跨历史的才预计算。
why_en: Take them straight from the request payload and session state with no external lookup, because they are derivable from the current request and need no history aggregation.
options: 预计算进特征库,和用户历史 CTR 一样对待
直接从请求 payload 和会话状态取,无需外部查,因为当前请求就能得出
从 30 天日志里聚合出来,每小时刷新一次
让客户端上传后再回写数据库,下次请求才用
options_en: Precompute into the feature store, treated like user historical CTR.
Take them directly from the request payload and session state with no lookup, since the current request yields them.
Aggregate them from 30-day logs, refreshed hourly.
Have the client upload them, write back to the database, and use them next request.
optionExplanations: 上下文特征当前请求就有,预计算它们纯属多此一举还引入陈旧。
对;时段/设备/槽位/会话状态都在请求里,直接读、零外部查,是延迟最省的实时特征。
这些不是历史聚合量,没必要从日志算,预计算反而更慢更旧。
回写再用引入一整轮延迟,当前请求就能取的信息没理由绕这么大圈。
optionExplanations_en: Context features are already in the current request; precomputing them is redundant and adds staleness.
Correct — time/device/slot/session state are in the request, read directly with zero lookup — the lowest-latency real-time features.
These are not history aggregations, so computing from logs is needless and precompute is slower and staler.
Write-back-then-use adds a whole round-trip of latency for info the current request already has.

termDefinitions.meaning: 广告请求本身携带的数据(时段、设备、广告位、槽位),实时特征直接从中读取。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The request payload is the data the ad request carries (time, device, placement, slot); real-time features read straight from it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 本次会话内的即时状态(已展示广告、上次点击),实时可得、无需外部查。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Session state is the in-session status (ads already shown, last click), available in real time with no external lookup.

scenario: 用户 3 分钟前刚点过某类广告,这个信号对 pCTR 很有价值。批处理特征每小时才刷一次,拿不到这么新的信息;请求路径又没法现算历史聚合。
scenario_en: A user clicked an ad type 3 minutes ago — valuable for pCTR. Batch features refresh hourly (too stale) and the request path cannot aggregate history live.
q: 怎么在延迟预算内拿到这种分钟级新鲜的聚合特征?
q_en: How do you get such minute-fresh aggregated features within budget?
why: 用流式管线(Kafka+Flink)做中间地带:它近实时地增量聚合最新事件,几分钟延迟就能反映「3 分钟前点过」,写进特征库供在线快查。它填补了批处理(小时/天,太旧)和纯请求实时(算不了历史聚合)之间的空档。
why_en: Use a streaming pipeline (Kafka+Flink) as the middle ground — it incrementally aggregates fresh events with minutes of delay into the feature store, bridging batch (too stale) and request-time real-time (can't aggregate history).
tradeoff: 流式(分钟级新鲜、增量聚合、多一套管线) vs 批处理(小时/天、简单但太旧)
whenOtherWins: 如果特征本身天级更新就够(如用户长期类目亲和),用便宜的批处理即可,不必上流式的复杂度。
options: 把批处理频率提高到每分钟一次,靠硬刷解决
用流式管线(Kafka+Flink)近实时增量聚合,分钟级写进特征库,填批处理和请求实时之间的空档
在请求路径上现扫日志算 3 分钟窗口聚合
干脆放弃这个信号,只用小时级批处理特征
options_en: Raise batch frequency to once per minute and brute-force refresh.
Use a streaming pipeline (Kafka+Flink) to incrementally aggregate near-real-time, writing minute-fresh into the feature store, bridging batch and request-time.
Scan logs on the request path to aggregate a 3-minute window live.
Just drop the signal and use only hourly batch features.
optionExplanations: 把批处理压到每分钟成本极高且仍是全量重算,不如增量流式高效。
对;Kafka+Flink 增量聚合最新事件,分钟级延迟写入特征库,在线快查即可,是批与纯实时之间的标准中间地带。
请求路径现算历史窗口必超 20ms 预算,正是流式要替代的做法。
放弃有价值的新鲜信号会损失精度,流式本可低成本拿到它。
optionExplanations_en: Compressing batch to per-minute is very costly and still full recompute, less efficient than incremental streaming.
Correct — Kafka+Flink incrementally aggregate fresh events into the feature store with minutes' delay for online lookup, the standard middle ground.
Live window aggregation on the request path blows the 20ms budget — exactly what streaming replaces.
Dropping a valuable fresh signal costs accuracy that streaming could capture cheaply.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式事件流平台,承载点击/曝光等实时事件,供 Flink 消费聚合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed event-streaming platform carrying real-time events like clicks/impressions for Flink to consume and aggregate.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式流处理引擎,对 Kafka 事件做近实时增量聚合,产出分钟级新鲜特征。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Flink is a distributed stream-processing engine that incrementally aggregates Kafka events into minute-fresh features.

scenario: 规模假设:10 亿用户、1000 万活跃广告、峰值 500K QPS。你要估算特征总存储。
scenario_en: Scale: 1B users, 10M active ads, 500K QPS peak. You estimate total feature storage.
q: 量化后特征总存储大概多少,怎么落地部署?
q_en: Roughly what is total feature storage after quantization, and how is it deployed?
why: 量化后总量约 270 GB:用户 embedding 64 GB(int8)+ 用户画像 200 GB + 广告 embedding 2.56 GB + 广告元数据 5 GB。这个量级放不进单机,要用分片 Redis 集群 + 副本来承载和保证可用。
why_en: About 270 GB after quantization (user embeddings 64 GB int8, user profiles 200 GB, ad embeddings 2.56 GB, ad metadata 5 GB), too big for one node, so a sharded Redis cluster with replication.
options: 约 4 GB,单台机器内存就能全放下
约 270 GB(量化后),放不进单机,用分片 Redis 集群 + 副本承载
约 10 TB,必须全部落磁盘、放弃内存服务
约 256 GB,且只有用户 embedding 一项,别的可忽略
options_en: About 4 GB, fitting entirely in one machine's memory.
About 270 GB after quantization, too big for one node, served by a sharded Redis cluster with replication.
About 10 TB, forced entirely onto disk, abandoning in-memory serving.
About 256 GB, and only user embeddings — everything else is negligible.
optionExplanations: 4 GB 远远不够,光量化后的用户 embedding 就 64 GB,加画像 200 GB。
对;各项相加约 270 GB,超单机内存,分片 Redis + 副本既扩容量又保可用,是标准落地。
10 TB 高估了,量化后是几百 GB 量级,仍可内存分片服务不必全落盘。
用户画像 200 GB 同样是大头,不能只算 embedding 忽略其余。
optionExplanations_en: 4 GB is far too little; quantized user embeddings alone are 64 GB plus 200 GB of profiles.
Correct — the parts sum to ~270 GB, over one node's memory, so a sharded Redis cluster with replicas scales capacity and availability — the standard deployment.
10 TB overestimates; after quantization it is hundreds of GB, still shardable in memory without going all-disk.
User profiles at 200 GB are also a big share; you cannot count only embeddings.

termDefinitions.term: sharded Redis cluster / 分片 Redis 集群
termDefinitions.meaning: 把特征数据按 key 切分到多台 Redis 节点,突破单机内存上限,加副本保可用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sharded Redis cluster splits feature data by key across nodes to exceed single-machine memory, with replicas for availability.

scenario: 峰值 500K QPS,每次广告请求平均要向特征库发约 3 次查询。
scenario_en: At 500K QPS peak, each ad request issues about 3 feature-store lookups.
q: 特征库要扛多大读吞吐,这个数怎么算、用来做什么?
q_en: What read throughput must the feature store sustain, how is it computed, and what for?
why: 公式:500K QPS × 3 次查询 = 150 万次读/秒;每次约 300 字节 → 约 450 MB/s。这个吞吐是估读侧规模的基数——据此推出需要约 10 节点的 Redis 集群配读副本才扛得住。
why_en: 500K QPS × 3 lookups = 1.5M reads/sec, ~300 B each → ~450 MB/s, the read-scale base that sizes the cluster (about 10 Redis nodes with read replicas).
options: 约 5 万次读/秒,单个 Redis 节点足够
约 150 万次读/秒(500K×3),约 450 MB/s,据此配约 10 节点 Redis + 读副本
约 500 次读/秒,与 QPS 无关
约 5 亿次读/秒,任何集群都扛不住,只能放弃特征库
options_en: About 50K reads/sec, one Redis node suffices.
About 1.5M reads/sec (500K×3), ~450 MB/s, sizing about 10 Redis nodes with read replicas.
About 500 reads/sec, unrelated to QPS.
About 500M reads/sec, unbearable for any cluster, so drop the feature store.
optionExplanations: 5 万远远低估,500K×3 就是 150 万次/秒,单节点扛不住。
对;150 万读/秒、约 450 MB/s 是读侧规模基数,直接推出约 10 节点 Redis + 读副本的部署。
500 次/秒完全脱离规模,QPS×每请求查询数才是真实吞吐。
5 亿是把量级夸大百倍,150 万/秒经分片副本完全可承载。
optionExplanations_en: 50K badly underestimates; 500K×3 is 1.5M/sec, beyond a single node.
Correct — 1.5M reads/sec and ~450 MB/s is the read-scale base, directly sizing ~10 Redis nodes with read replicas.
500/sec ignores scale entirely; QPS × lookups-per-request is the real throughput.
500M inflates by 100×; 1.5M/sec is fully serviceable via sharding and replicas.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每秒请求数;这里峰值 500K QPS,乘以每请求查询数得到特征库读吞吐。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: QPS (Queries Per Second) is requests per second; here 500K QPS times lookups-per-request gives feature-store read throughput.

termDefinitions.meaning: 主节点数据的只读拷贝,用来分摊读吞吐、提高可用性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A read replica is a read-only copy of a primary's data used to spread read throughput and improve availability.

scenario: 峰值 500K QPS,若每次请求都要给约 200 个候选广告用完整模型打分。
scenario_en: At 500K QPS peak, if each request scores about 200 candidate ads with the full model.
q: 这会产生多大的打分量,推出什么架构决策?
q_en: How many scores does this produce, and what architectural decision follows?
why: 500K QPS × 200 候选 = 每秒 1 亿次模型打分。这个量级下不可能对所有候选都跑重模型,正是为什么必须两段式:先便宜检索把上千候选收窄,只对约 200 个跑排序模型。
why_en: 500K QPS × 200 candidates = 100M model scores/sec, which no heavy model can serve for all candidates — exactly why two-stage retrieval-then-ranking is essential.
options: 每秒约 50 万次打分,单模型轻松扛得住,不需要两段式
每秒约 1 亿次打分(500K×200),重模型扛不住全部,所以必须两段式只排约 200 候选
每秒约 200 次打分,和 QPS 无关
每秒约 1000 亿次打分,任何硬件都不可能,只能不做 CTR 排序
options_en: About 500K scores/sec, easily handled by one model, no two-stage needed.
About 100M scores/sec (500K×200), unbearable for a heavy model on all, so two-stage ranking of ~200 candidates is essential.
About 200 scores/sec, unrelated to QPS.
About 100 billion scores/sec, impossible for any hardware, so skip CTR ranking.
optionExplanations: 50 万漏乘了候选数,真实是 500K×200=1 亿次/秒,单模型全量打分扛不住。
对;1 亿次/秒的打分逼出两段式——检索先粗筛,重模型只打约 200 个候选,才进得了延迟与算力预算。
200 次/秒完全脱离规模,QPS×候选数才是真实打分量。
1000 亿高估了三个数量级,1 亿次/秒经两段式完全可行。
optionExplanations_en: 500K omits the candidate factor; the real figure is 500K×200=100M/sec, beyond one model scoring all.
Correct — 100M scores/sec forces two-stage: retrieval coarse-filters and the heavy model scores only ~200, fitting latency and compute.
200/sec ignores scale; QPS × candidates is the real score count.
100 billion overstates by three orders; 100M/sec is feasible via two-stage.

termDefinitions.term: model scores per second / 每秒打分量
termDefinitions.meaning: QPS × 每请求候选数,衡量推理侧总负载,过高时逼出两段式检索-排序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Model scores per second is QPS times candidates-per-request, the inference-side load that forces two-stage retrieval-ranking when high.

scenario: 面试官抛出杀手锏追问:「你怎么给十亿用户在 20ms 内提供用户特征?」
scenario_en: The interviewer drops the killer follow-up: 'How do you serve user features for a billion users under 20ms?'
q: 该怎么组织这套回答的骨架?
q_en: How do you structure the backbone of this answer?
why: 骨架三件套:①贵的历史聚合特征预计算进特征库(p99 <5-10ms 快查)、②高基数 embedding 用哈希/量化压进服务节点内存、③按 key 分片 Redis + 副本扛 150 万读/秒。上下文特征则从请求实时取。把「预计算+压缩+分片」串起来正面回答延迟与规模。
why_en: Precompute history features into a low-latency feature store, compress high-cardinality embeddings (hashing/quantization) to fit serving memory, and shard Redis with replicas for throughput — while context features come real-time from the request.
tradeoff: 预计算+压缩+分片(20ms 内可服务十亿用户) vs 请求路径现算(简单但必超时)
whenOtherWins: 如果用户量只有百万级、特征也不大,单个内存 KV 直接查就够,不必上分片+压缩这套重装。
options: 每次请求现算用户历史聚合,靠加机器把延迟压到 20ms
预计算进特征库快查 + 压缩 embedding 进内存 + 分片 Redis 配副本扛吞吐,上下文特征实时取
把所有用户特征塞进模型权重,推理时不查任何外部存储
让每个用户请求时同步训练一个专属小模型
options_en: Aggregate user history live on each request and add machines to hit 20ms.
Precompute into a fast feature store + compress embeddings into memory + sharded Redis with replicas for throughput, with context features real-time.
Bake all user features into model weights so inference queries no external store.
Synchronously train a per-user model on each request.
optionExplanations: 现算历史聚合扫日志必超 20ms,加机器也压不进请求路径的重聚合。
对;预计算+压缩+分片三管齐下,把历史特征快查、embedding 放进内存、吞吐用副本扛,正面解掉延迟与规模。
把十亿用户特征塞进权重不现实,模型会爆炸且无法更新用户级信息。
每请求训模型完全不可行,延迟和成本都无穷大。
optionExplanations_en: Live history aggregation scans logs and must exceed 20ms; machines cannot fit heavy aggregation on the request path.
Correct — precompute + compress + shard together fast-lookup history, fit embeddings in memory, and sustain throughput via replicas, directly solving latency and scale.
Baking a billion users' features into weights is unrealistic; the model explodes and cannot update user-level info.
Per-request model training is infeasible, with unbounded latency and cost.

termDefinitions.term: feature serving under latency / 低延迟特征服务
termDefinitions.meaning: 在几十毫秒内为海量用户提供特征的能力,靠预计算、压缩和分片三者组合实现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Low-latency feature serving is delivering features for massive user bases within tens of ms, achieved by combining precompute, compression, and sharding.
